rationale: Microsoft-authored MCP server wrapping Playwright browser automation as MCP tools. Exposes 25+ tools (navigate, click, type, snapshot, evaluate, network interception, storage, PDF, devtools, vision/coordinates) via the Model Context Protocol. Ranked B (not S/A) because: (1) the actual automation source code lives upstream in the Playwright monorepo (packages/playwright-core/src/tools/mcp) not in this checkout -- this package is a thin distribution shim (index.js is 2 lines re-exporting from playwright-core/lib/coreBundle), making local architectural depth minimal; (2) no JSON-LD extraction, self-healing selectors, stealth, queue, fuzzy-matching, or fulltext-search concerns are addressed; (3) has CI/CD, Docker support, multi-browser testing (Chrome/Firefox/WebKit), and typed config. Relevant to browser-automation concern directly. Scores 7.5: essential if the pipeline uses MCP-based orchestration, but a containing project may also use Playwright directly without this MCP layer.
limitations: Source code is NOT in this checkout; actual implementation lives upstream at https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/tree/main/packages/playwright-core/src/tools/mcp -- local files are distribution artifacts only (cli.js wraps program from playwright-core/lib/coreBundle).
No architecture or design documentation present locally; src/ directory contains only a README pointing upstream.
No self-healing selector logic, stealth/anti-bot measures, JSON-LD extraction, fuzzy matching, fulltext search, or queue/job scheduling -- covers only browser-automation among pipeline concerns.
No script generation from natural language; codegen is limited to emitting Playwright test code for actions taken (--codegen typescript).
Depends on pre-release playwright-core 1.62.0-alpha, not a stable release.
Docker support limited to headless Chromium only.
